reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage XGold with a claimed 1,200% profit from a $10 starting amount and displays large projected returns. It instructs viewers to open slots, repeatedly reinvest, join the speaker's team, recruit two people, and contact a WhatsApp network team for participation.

opening.argument: Judge the claims as forecasts, not a promise of an available, guaranteed payout. The speaker says there is no fixed launch date and directs viewers to a calculator of potential results. Even the large figure is conditional on members duplicating across four levels. That uncertainty matters when deciding whether the video establishes a deceptive guarantee.

citations.quote: There are no fixed date for the launch of xGold
It has Exgoal Calculator you can take a look at the 1st, 2nd, and even 3rd shot which potentials will we get
if you have 2 members that can duplicate the 4 levels and together increase the slot from only one slot to the 15th slot

rebuttal.rebuttal: The quoted instructions describe how a proposed team arrangement would work; they do not establish that anyone has received the stated sum. The invitation to contact the speaker is concerning, but the speaker also says the launch date is not fixed. The opening treats projected earnings as though they were an established outcome.

citations.quote: when you join my team, you get 7,329,765,000 Rupiah only by just 2 people.
There are no fixed date for the launch of xGold

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An uncertain launch date does not qualify the earnings pitch. The speaker calls the projected profit 1,200%, tells viewers that duplicating members through four levels will yield profit, and invites them to join his team for a stated payout. The issue is the promoted recruitment-based earning mechanism, not proof that a payout has already occurred.

opening.argument: Much of the presentation is an operational walkthrough. The speaker introduces it as a review, points viewers to a calculator they can inspect, and explains how returns vary by slot and by the number of members at each level. A judge can recognize the team invitation without reducing the entire video to that invitation: the detailed explanation of the matrix is central to what viewers receive.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies a team invitation, but an invitation does not erase the extended explanation of how the slots and levels operate. The speaker explicitly offers to explain the viewer's two-member arrangement. Those details support reading the video as a tutorial with promotional elements, rather than treating every explanation as a direct instruction to participate.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough teaches viewers how to generate income through recruiting members. The speaker recommends duplicating two members through four levels, says that will produce profit, and asks interested viewers to join his team. The demonstration is part of the promotion, not an independent lesson about a tool.

IF YOU WANT TO BE A PART OF MY TEAM THESE ARE 3 SLOTS

opening.argument: The described activity can also be read as a referral promotion with priced slots: the speaker discusses a starting amount, explains member formation, and calls the activity a business without a deposit. He asks viewers to contact him, but the supplied statements do not show a credential request or a completed transfer. The evidence establishes a sales pitch and a referral structure; those facts alone do not verify that viewers' money has been taken or that the described payouts cannot occur.

citations.quote: X Gold starts with $10 to open one by one
this is the business for such global trading non-local without a deposit
You can get 2 member formation We got the 2 member duplicated
my whatsapp number is in the description you just have to click it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's quotes establish recruitment and projected earnings, but not an observed payment, credential handover, or realized loss. The speaker's phrase about operating without a deposit complicates the claim that this excerpt documents a deposit-taking scheme. The judge should distinguish the mechanism being advertised from proof of what happens after someone joins.

citations.quote: this is the business for such global trading non-local without a deposit
when you join my team, you get 7,329,765,000 Rupiah only by just 2 people.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed loss or credential request is not required to identify the pitch. The speaker links profits to recruiting members across successive rings, urges viewers to duplicate members through four levels, and offers paid slots as a way into his team. Calling it a business without a deposit does not change that advertised mechanism.
